stage1Boundary: Stage 1 validates the backend -> provider transformation only. Browser-side prompt assembly happens in the frontend before the request reaches the route and is NOT covered here; a green provider-wire capture is not evidence of preset-level equivalence.

tier2.reason: The mock listens on an ephemeral loopback port, so the authority is not a property of either backend.
tier2.harnessSource: tools/mock-provider/main.go: --port 0 asks the kernel for a free port

tier2.rule: value replaced with Bearer <redacted>, presence and scheme preserved
tier2.reason: The scenario supplies a synthetic key; presence and scheme are the contract and the value is asserted by expectedAuthorizationKey.

tier2.rule: the recorder origin is replaced with <mock>, the PATH is kept
tier2.reason: API_PERPLEXITY is a pinned literal, so the pinned leg reaches the recorder through the transport redirect and the Go leg through GOTAVERN_PERPLEXITY_CHAT_URL. The path /chat/completions IS compared.

tier3.reason: A measurement of elapsed wall-clock time differs on every run; the value is a duration, not a contract.

name: perplexity-missing-key
purpose: PERPLEXITY with NO api_key_perplexity: the branch reads the secret unconditionally (:2424) and the shared guard at :2615 answers 400 { error: true } WITHOUT calling the provider, so the mock script is empty by design. The frontend records PERPLEXITY in noValidateSources (openai.js:4459), which is about the CONNECT button only, so this refusal is the GENERATE path and is recorded rather than derived.
